City council approves riverfront park plan after “marathon” session

By María José Álvarez and John E. Smith

The city council voted 7-2 late Tuesday to approve a long-debated plan to convert six acres of former rail yard into a riverfront park, ending months of public hearings and revisions.

Supporters packed the chamber for the vote, which came after nearly five hours of public comment. Several residents said the park would give their neighborhoods their first direct access to the water in generations.

Opponents, including two council members, argued that the project's budget relied on optimistic projections for state grants and that the city should prioritize road repairs and other maintenance that has been deferred for years.

The approved plan includes a walking and cycling path, a small amphitheater, native plantings intended to manage stormwater runoff, and a boat launch. Construction is expected to begin next spring and take roughly two years.

City staff said they will return to the council in January with a detailed financing schedule and a timeline for community meetings on the park's final design, including the playground and public art elements.

The mayor, who has championed the project since taking office, called the vote a turning point for the downtown waterfront and thanked residents who had spent their evenings at hearings over the last year.
